instruction:
Herringbone Parquet Floor

Read `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\params.json`; it has these fields:
- `floor_width`, `floor_height`: floor dimensions in metres (2.4 x 1.8 m).
- `plank_length`, `plank_width`, `plank_thickness`: plank dimensions in metres (0.8 x 0.2 x 0.015 m).
- `pattern_angle_deg`: rotation of the herringbone pattern relative to world axes (45 deg).

tile the 2.4 x 1.8 m rectangle in world XY (with Z up, base at Z = 0) with a herringbone-pattern parquet floor made of identical 0.2 x 0.8 x 0.015 m planks, all referencing ONE shared ComponentDefinition. The planks alternate between +45 deg and -45 deg (equivalently +135 deg) orientations around the world Z axis so their long axes lie along world X+Y and world X-Y respectively; this produces the classic herringbone zig-zag visible when you look down at the floor. Each plank's short end should meet a perpendicular neighbour's edge at a right angle, and no two planks overlap (in their actual XY footprint) by more than 1% of a single plank's area.

Export the result to `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp`. The DAE must contain exactly one `<geometry>` entry in `<library_geometries>` (the canonical plank) plus one `<node>` in the scene graph per plank, each referencing that one geometry via `<instance_geometry>` and carrying a (translate + rotate-Z) transform that places the plank at its world location.

Pass conditions (evaluated against `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp`):
1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\answer.skp` can be opened and inspected as a native SketchUp model.
2. Exactly one distinct geometry id is referenced by scene `<node>` entries.
3. At least 15 scene instances reference that geometry.
4. About half of the instances have their long axis along world +45 deg and the other half along +135 deg (each class must be at least 35% of the total; no other angles permitted within 2 deg tolerance).
5. The overall world-space bounding box of the plank collection fits the expected 2.4 x 1.8 m floor footprint at the origin within 10 cm (both in position and in span).
6. Every plank has a world-space Z extent of exactly 0.015 m within 0.5 mm (i.e. planks are flat, not thick columns).
7. No two planks' oriented (XY) footprints overlap by more than 1% of a single plank's area (0.16 m^2).
source: [Chopra-Architect] herringbone parquet floor geometry; SU-Ruby `ComponentDefinition.add` + `Geom::Transformation.rotation`; COLLADA 1.5 library_geometries + instance_geometry
